g4ela-27-1-morphology: Some words are built on old Latin bases. Port means carry, so a porter carries bags. Tract means pull, so a tractor pulls a plow. Struct means build, so a structure is something built. Find the base, ask what it does, and set a treasure back in its place.
g4ela-27-2-grammar: But and so are tiny hinges. But says, here comes a surprise: Caspian’s heart was sinking, but he tried to take it all in. So says, here’s what happened because of it. Put a comma before each when it joins two whole sentences.
g4ela-27-3-spelling: Here’s a trick for long words. Say the word and listen for the strong beat. Be-GIN. If the beat is on the last part, and it ends in one vowel and one consonant, double the consonant: beginning. VIS-it has its beat at the front, so no double: visiting.
g4ela-27-4-grammar: Editing day. Read each sentence with but or so, and ask if the logic is right. Caspian was tired, but he rode on. That works. Caspian was tired, so he rode on. That doesn’t. One small word, and the meaning flips.
